title: Angola Pulse (Pulso Angola) - BRAZIL: ANGOLA PULSE
style:
```
[style: Afro-Brazilian Angola capoeira, berimbau musical bow three tones, surdo bass drum two-beat, atabaque conga, pandeiro frame drum tie, 6/8 over 4/4 Candomblé Angola 3:2, capoeira ginga rhythm, Bahia ceremonial spirit, Portuguese spoken verses English chorus, African signal surviving crossing theme, body-as-signal metaphor, no electronic elements, V4_5ALL]
```
lyrics:
`
[INTRO — berimbau only, single note struck and muted, capoeira ginga rhythm]
(Portuguese) Angola — the origin / the signal that crossed the water

[VERSE 1 — atabaque enters, then pandeiro]
(Portuguese) O arame — the wire / the berimbau string
(English)    One string / one bow / one gourd
(Portuguese) Três contra dois — three against two
(English)    The signal that survived the crossing

The berimbau says three while the surdo says two
The pandeiro ties the knot — between me and you
Candomblé Angola — the oldest African pulse
That arrived in Brazil and never stopped the pulse

(Portuguese) Capoeira — the fight is also a dance
(English)    The signal moves in the body

[PRE-CHORUS — berimbau accelerates, capoeira call-and-response implied]
(Portuguese) Iê — the capoeira call
(English)    The master signals
(Portuguese) Camará — companion / partner
(English)    The answer signals back

[CHORUS — surdo drops heavy, pandeiro rolls]
Angola pulse — three against two
The berimbau crossed the water / brought the rhythm through
Surdo holds the ground / berimbau holds the sky
The 3:2 signal lives — and never asks you why

(Portuguese) Rio abaixo — downstream
(English)    The signal flows

[VERSE 2 — berimbau three tones: open, muted, press — demonstrated]
The berimbau has three notes
Open: the highest
Muted: the middle
Pressed coin on string: the lowest
Three notes. Three pitches. Three against two.
The crossing was not the end — it was the opening of the three

(Portuguese) Travessia — crossing / passage
(English)    The signal that crossed became

[BRIDGE — all instruments on the 3:2 simultaneously, 16 bars]
Count with me:
Three: DUM da DUM da DUM da
Two: BOOM — — BOOM — —
Together: they share beats 1 and 4
That is where Africa and Brazil meet
That is the Angola pulse
That is the signal

[FINAL CHORUS — doubled, all instruments in full Angola Candomblé rhythm]
Angola pulse — three against two

[OUTRO — berimbau muted to silence, surdo one last BOOM]
(Portuguese) Axé — life force / the signal is alive
